characteristics: amphibious on early models (5-7km/h in water)
Strength: Simple, extremely widely produced design with a huge global logistics/parts base
Limitation: 1960s-era design, minimal armor by modern standards, primarily a battlefield taxi rather than a fighting vehicle
Estimated quantity available: Donated in significant numbers across multiple donor nations; exact total not fully disclosed
employment_notes: Represents the largest single category of Western-donated tracked vehicles by volume, used to move infantry and casualties rather than fight from
contrast_vs_traditional: A Vietnam-era design still in front-line use isn't a survivability story — it's an attrition-economics one. On a battlefield where the doctrine.md figure puts 60–70% of equipment losses on drones rather than direct fire, a simple, numerous, cheaply replaceable carrier is arguably better matched to the loss rate than a more exquisite platform would be, which is not the reasoning that put it in service originally.
